prove_sample.question: can a bounded agent prove the label of a random row?
prove_sample.frame: solutions/, no proof in solutions-proved/, non-empty label
prove_sample.note_on_contradiction: Empty by construction. Every proof in this campaign is an upper bound; contradicting a label needs a lower bound, which none of them produces. A bound above the label is `looser`, not a disagreement.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: real-number tuple-sort quantifiers combined with a nonlinear Pow2 bound. The agent also suspects the true charged cost is quadratic, but never closed a proof, so that suspicion is not evidence.
rows.why_failed: Solve mixes real-number tuple-sort quantifiers (forall x in ratios/d) with the new nonlinear Pow2Cost/SortCost step arithmetic in one VC; Z3 does not close it even at 3x the time budget. Note: the real obstacle here is more than proof technique -- Pow2_140 is linear recursion (not squaring), so this row's true charged cost is O(n^2), genuinely disagreeing with its O(nlogn) label, but that disagreement was never machine-checked because the surrounding VC would not close.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: the chained bound needs three multiplication facts at once; isolating each did not close the chain.
rows.why_failed: the final chained bound needs each multiplication (SortCost(|c|)<=..., |c|<=2|s|, CeilLog2 monotonicity) isolated into its own lemma the way solutions-proved/nlogn/603_284 does; combining them in inline asserts made the nonlinear arithmetic too much for Z3 within the time limit

rows.label: O(n)
rows.relation_reason: the proved cost contains a binary search over the VALUE a*b, not over the query count. Whether a loop bounded by a capped value counts as constant is the open value-versus-size convention.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: merge sort charged with the loose O(k^2) scaffold; the agent states the tight O(k log k) bound was not attempted. Nothing here bears on the label.

rows.label: O(n)
rows.relation_reason: proves 6*|numbers|*MaxLen(numbers)+... because comparing a string against a running best costs per-character. Whether string length is a size parameter is the same open convention.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: SortCost/CeilLog2 bound verifies standalone; times out combined with the SumSizes additive term in one VC.
rows.why_failed: Z3 cannot combine the SortCost/CeilLog2 nonlinear recursion-tree bound with the additive SumSizes(ans-length) threading in Solve's single verification condition; the two arguments verify individually but not together within the time limit, and the opaque/{:opaque}+reveal split that fixed the same timeout in 2188_359 and 2426_4 was not tried before the budget ran out.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: same sort scaffold as 1421_89. Proof slack, not a label finding.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: sort bound verifies as a standalone lemma; the surrounding method's VC does not close in 30s.
rows.why_failed: even with the sort's own nonlinear bound isolated and verified as a standalone lemma, the surrounding method (two flag loops + two RemoveFirst charges + branch merge) still made the combined postcondition VC too large for Z3 in 30s; needs the whole linear+log combination split into one more helper lemma taking the raw steps arithmetic out of the method body

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.relation_reason: quadratic base bound plus a further (n+2)*idx term would not combine into the n^2 postcondition.
rows.why_failed: the postcondition needs base1 (itself a quadratic-in-n bound) combined with a further (n+2)*idx term to prove <= a single n^2 coefficient; Z3 won't do this nonlinear combination without isolated MulMonoRight/MulDistrib-style lemmas, which weren't written before the budget ran out.

rows.label: O(1)
rows.relation_reason: the invariant mechanism was found; it ran out of its 3 attempts one edit short of the final case split. Expected to close with more budget.
rows.why_failed: needed one more edit (an explicit if/else on hitFound after the inner loop to select the right half of the split invariant) -- the mechanism is right, just short one attempt

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: square-monotonicity (a<=b ==> a*a<=b*b) would not discharge even isolated.
rows.why_failed: Z3 would not close a square-monotonicity lemma (a<=b ==> a*a<=b*b) needed to lift SortCost's per-element O(k^2) bound to a bound in terms of n; combined with this row's pre-existing per-index exists/forall invariants, Solve times out at 30s independent of that lemma.

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.relation_reason: the array is sized r+1 where r grows by arbitrary input values. No bound in n alone exists without a new precondition, which the brief forbids. Same convention as the looser-structural rows.
rows.why_failed: structural: the array arr has size r+1, and r starts at m then grows by pos[pi].1 (an arbitrary input value) in the first loop, so the array size -- and the cost of the inner 'while j<=r' loop, run |neg| times -- has no bound expressible in n or m alone without an unstated assumption on the input's magnitudes (the file's own header notes r reaches ~30000 only in this row's own test data, not structurally). No requires may be added to fix that domain, so no n-parameterized ensures is provable; skipped straight to unresolved rather than burn attempts on an unprovable postcondition.

rows.label: O(n)
rows.bound: 40 * n + 3 * SumFirst(pairs, n) + 4, where SumFirst sums each test case's own n-value

rows.label: O(1)
rows.relation_reason: IntToString costs the digit count of n, i.e. log of the value. Constant only if the value is treated as capped.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: isolating the |arr| vs |pairs|+1 substitution into its own lemma did not help.
rows.why_failed: even isolating the |arr| vs |pairs|+1 substitution into its own trivial lemma didn't help -- the timeout is at the whole-method VC, suggesting Z3 retries nonlinear search across the combined SortCost unfolding + CeilLog2 + linear steps terms together rather than at any one identified step; would need the whole postcondition's arithmetic moved into one dedicated closing lemma taking steps as a parameter

rows.label: O(n)
rows.relation_reason: the third loop's range comes from input values with no requires tying it to n, so the bound carries 4*max(0, hi-lo) beyond the linear term.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: same sort scaffold as 1421_89. Proof slack, not a label finding.

rows.label: O(n*m)
rows.relation_reason: n's sign is unconstrained in the original signature, so no i<=n invariant holds. Needs a precondition the brief forbids inventing.
rows.why_failed: n's sign is unconstrained (no requires n>=0 in the original), so a plain i<=n invariant fails at loop entry for negative n; the fix (mirror 457_27's if-n>=0-else-0 defensive invariant plus a matching conditional ensures) was identified but not applied within the attempt budget. Separately: the true bound here is O(n), not O(n*m) -- x is capped at 2008 by the fixed-size table |d|==2009, so the label's 'm' is a hard constant in this row.
